title: Changing the customer on a Part Sale keeps its prices and shows the notice
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Settings — Parts', 'See Financial Data', 'Customers — View', 'Customers — Create & Edit' and 'Part Sales — Create & Edit'.
  • Have a new category for this test, category A, priced by a new matrix for this test, matrix A, with one cost range ($0.00 and up) whose Default rule is Markup % 35.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier A, with a name no other tier uses, whose column in matrix A is % Off 10.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier B, with a name no other tier uses, whose column in matrix A is % Off 20.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, put on tier A for Part Sales in Edit Customer.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, put on tier B for Part Sales in Edit Customer.
  • Have a new Part Sale for this test, Part Sale 1, for customer A, made after customer A's tiers were set, with a part in category A priced $121.50 by tier A.
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so every column of the page shows.
custom_steps:
1. Open Part Sale 1.
  2. Click Change Customer in the Part Sale's three-dot menu.
  3. Pick customer B.
  4. Click Update Customer.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part Sale 1 opens with the part at $121.50.

Step 2:

  • Change Customer opens with "Parts already on the Part Sale keep their prices, and new parts keep this Part Sale's pricing."

Step 3:

  • An amber note says this Part Sale keeps tier A pricing and tier B applies to new Part Sales.

Step 4:

  • Part Sale 1 names customer B and its part still reads $121.50.
  • A notice says 1 line was priced at tier A for the previous customer.
